content: Understanding the importance of community engagement is critical in controlling the spread of Ebola virus disease (EVD). The following outlines the key principles and procedures for managing contact tracing during an Ebola outbreak, as well as the roles and responsibilities of team members involved in this process. Purpose of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) The purpose of these SOPs is to define the structure and responsibilities of the Contact Tracing Team, which is tasked with monitoring individuals who have been in contact with confirmed EVD cases. Once an EVD case is identified, an investigation generates a list of contacts. If any contact develops symptoms of EVD, they are immediately isolated, referred for testing, and further investigated. These SOPs are based on the CDC-WHO Emergency Guidelines for Contact Tracing and have been adapted using WHO technical guidance and input from Ebola preparedness teams. They must be tailored to the specific local context. Human Resource Requirements The following personnel are required for effective contact tracing: Lead Epidemiologist: Oversees all operations, including investigations, staff training, and resource mobilization. Field Epidemiologists: Manage overall contact tracing performance and assign contacts to supervisors. Supervisors: Oversee 5–10 Contact Follow-Up Teams and provide field support. Contact Follow-Up Teams: Composed of two members per team, with the number of teams varying based on the number of contacts. Data Managers: Handle data entry and analysis. Drivers: Provide transportation for field teams. Equipment and Materials Requirements The following items are essential for contact tracing operations: Definitions of cases and contacts. Contact tracing forms. Alcohol-based hand sanitizers. Reliable communication devices, such as cell phones. Dedicated vehicles for fieldwork. Daily Operations 1. The Field Epidemiologist meets with Supervisors to distribute an updated contact list. 2. Supervisors meet with Contact Follow-Up Teams to distribute contact tracing forms, review the previous day’s activities, and address areas for improvement. 3. Supervisors and Contact Follow-Up Teams proceed with fieldwork. 4. At the end of the day, the Contact Follow-Up Teams submit their forms to the Supervisor, who synthesizes the data into a summary report. Any missing contacts are reviewed and highlighted. 5. The summary report is sent to the Data Manager and Field Epidemiologist for electronic entry and analysis. 6. The Lead Epidemiologist reviews the data and shares the summary report and analysis with partners. Team Member Responsibilities Lead Epidemiologist Oversees all operations, including investigations, staff training, and resource mobilization. Supervises Field Epidemiologists. Updates committee leaders within the Incident Management Framework. Field Epidemiologist Manages overall contact tracing performance. Assigns contacts to Supervisors and generates the daily contact list, incorporating new contacts. Identifies contacts not followed the previous day as priorities. Supervises data entry and performs data analysis. Supervisor Distributes updated contact tracing forms to Contact Follow-Up Teams daily. Assigns new contacts to teams and provides field support. Synthesizes data collected by teams into a daily summary report. Contact Follow-Up Team During the first visit, establishes trust and provides the contact with their phone number and a hotline number, if available. Answers any questions from the contact during the follow-up process. Meets each contact daily as per the list provided by the Supervisor. Submits completed forms to the Supervisor at the end of daily fieldwork. Immediately informs the Supervisor if a contact develops symptoms. Investigation Team Interviews potential cases and identifies all contacts of a case. Assesses symptomatic contacts to determine if they meet the case definition. By adhering to these structured procedures and clearly defined roles, the Contact Tracing Team can effectively monitor and manage the spread of Ebola virus disease, ensuring timely intervention and containment.
